identity.title: Pressure Profiles and Mass Estimates Using High-resolution Sunyaev-Zel'dovich Effect Observations of Zwicky 3146 with MUSTANG-2

paper_type_evidence.quote: data taken at 90 GHz by MUSTANG-2 to a noise level better than $15\ \mu$K at the center, and a cluster detection of $104\sigma$.
This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA#2011.0.00001.CAL.

evidence.quote: The galaxy cluster Zwicky 3146 is a sloshing cool core cluster at $z=0.291$
At $z=0.291$, one arcsecond corresponds to 4.36 kpc.

question.value: Can MUSTANG-2 90 GHz SZ data constrain the pressure profile and mass (M500, M2500) of the relaxed cluster Zwicky 3146, and how consistent are different mass estimators?

evidence.quote: Here, we investigate the ability to estimate the mass of Zwicky 3146 via the Sunyaev-Zel’dovich (SZ) effect with data taken at 90 GHz by MUSTANG-2

bands.value: MUSTANG-2 90 GHz on the GBT (not ALMA)

evidence.quote: Observing at 90 GHz on the 100-meter Robert C. Byrd Green Bank Telescope (GBT), MUSTANG-2 achieves a resolution of 10$''$
have a RMS noise of $15~\mu$K (when smoothed to beam resolution) within the central $2\ensuremath{'}$ radius
with a total on-source integration time of 22.7 hours. Excising bad scans, our final maps incorporate 21.4 hours of data
GBT data was taken under the project ID AGBT18A_175.

provided.value: 90 GHz SZ data for all main results

evidence.quote: Observing at 90 GHz on the 100-meter Robert C. Byrd Green Bank Telescope (GBT), MUSTANG-2 achieves a resolution of 10$''$

provided.value: electron density profile for hydrostatic masses and temperature/entropy

evidence.quote: In this work, we make use of an electron density profile from *XMM* (cite: ghirardini2018).

provided.value: grid calibrators used for MUSTANG-2 flux calibration

evidence.quote: We additionally use ALMA grid calibrators (cite: fomalont2014; vanKempen2014)
we make use of an electron density profile from *XMM* (cite: ghirardini2018).
There are six radio sources identified by FIRST (cite: becker1994) which correspond to sources found in the MUSTANG-2 maps.

flux_calibrator.value: Mars, Uranus, Jupiter, Saturn, Ceres, plus ALMA grid calibrators

evidence.quote: Absolute flux calibrations are preferentially based on the Solar System objects Mars, Uranus, Jupiter, Saturn, and Ceres.
Our observational techniques and data reduction are largely the same as with MUSTANG (cite: romero2015a; romero2017).

what.value: gNFW shape parameters alpha, beta, gamma fixed to A10 values

evidence.quote: we choose to fix $\alpha$, $\beta$, and $\gamma$ to their respective values found in (cite: arnaud2010) (hereafter, A10): 1.05, 5.41, and 0.31

unstated_but_needed: MCMC settings and priors for pressure profile fits
Y-M relation parameters (tabulated A,B but sources unnamed in text)

analysis_steps.goal: Map TODs with Minkasi and fit surface brightness annuli

method.value: Maximum-likelihood fit of concentric annuli to TODs, PCG solver, deconvolved profile with covariance

evidence.quote: we opt to fit a surface brightness profile directly to the MUSTANG-2 timestreams within the Minkasi pipeline.
We find sufficient convergence with 30 to 60 steps in the PCG.
A comparison of the performance between the two approaches is in Appendix [11](#sec:appendix_midas_minkasi)

analysis_steps.goal: Fit pressure profiles (NP and gNFW) with point sources

method.value: Compton y profile to T_B, matched to Minkasi bins with full covariance; 12 NP bins 5'' to 5'; A10 gNFW

evidence.quote: We define twelve bins with twelve logarithmically spaced radii between 5$''$ and 5$'$.

key_parameters.value: relativistic correction with kT_e = 7 keV; line of sight integration to ±5 R500

evidence.quote: we assume $k_B T_e = 7$ keV
The choice of adopting spherical symmetry is motivated by (1) the ease of interpretation of results and comparison to the literature

fitting.value: emcee MCMC with full covariance likelihood

evidence.quote: In both cases, the fitting is done with the MCMC package `emcee` (cite: foreman2013).
The pressure profile recovered is in excellent agreement with the pressure profile derived from *XMM*.

method.value: Y-M relations, hydrostatic equilibrium with XMM n_e, virial theorem; self-consistent R500 at each MCMC step

evidence.quote: We investigate mass estimates via three avenues: (1) employing a $Y$-$M$ relation, (2) employing spherical hydrostatic equilibrium (HE) and (3) employing the virial theorem (VT)
we take $\mu_e = 1.17$ and $f_{\text{gas}} = 0.13$.

assumptions.value: NFW matter profile for VT; central 100 kpc excluded

evidence.quote: We exclude the points within the central 100 kpc

fitting.value: VT: scipy curve fit for rho0 and 1/Rs, 1000 iterations

evidence.quote: $M_{500}$ is calculated self-consistently from the NFW mass curve (as for the hydrostatic mass) over 1000 iterations

used_for.value: maximum-likelihood TOD map and profile fitting

evidence.quote: the second method is a maximum likelihood approach (Minkasi).
The first method, called the MUSTANG IDL Data Analysis System (MIDAS)
the fitting is done with the MCMC package `emcee` (cite: foreman2013).
We obtain photometry of point sources from the level 2 maps with `photutils`
We take our fiducial mass to be $8.16^{+0.44}_{-0.54}$ ($\pm 5.5$% stat)
our estimate from hydrostatic equilibrium, is $8.29^{+1.93}_{-1.24}$
we find a peak decrement of $1002 \pm 70$ $\mu$K
$\alpha_{\text{NP}} = 1.34 \pm 0.06$

findings_qualitative.value: Pressure profile constrained to better than 15% out to 240'' (twice radial FOV) and matches XMM

evidence.quote: achieving constraints on the pressure profile to better than 15% out to 240$''$, or twice our radial FOV, is a marked improvement.

claims.hypothesis: Can Minkasi recover pressure profile beyond the FOV?
claims.experiment: Fit NP and gNFW profiles to TODs

evidence.quote: The pressure profile recovered is in excellent agreement with the pressure profile derived from *XMM*.

claims.hypothesis: Are mass estimators consistent with each other and with lensing?
claims.experiment: Y-M, HE, VT masses compared with literature

evidence.quote: this corresponds to only a $2\sigma$ discrepancy with the latest weak lensing measurement (cite: okabe2016).

limitations_admitted.value: Outermost pressure bin likely biased low; unquantified additional systematic

evidence.quote: there is an additional systematic error due the issues discussed in the previous two paragraphs, but which we are currently unable to quantify.

referee_caveats_inferred: Hydrostatic bias comes out negative, suggesting problems in data or Y-M relations
